<p class="page-deck">A public-evidence methodology for understanding occupation switching in the United Kingdom's low-carbon transition. It distinguishes same-occupation sector changes from occupation transitions and develops transparent approaches to occupational relatedness, transition requirements, calibration and evidence governance.</p>

**Status:** In Development<br>
**Relationship to the lab:** Current Lab Research — Owner-approved current programme of the Cities and Climate Learning Lab.<br>
**Primary theme:** [Consequences for People and Places](/research/consequences-for-people-and-places.html)

## How this project contributes to climate learning

**Primary theme:** [Consequences for People and Places](/research/consequences-for-people-and-places.html)

**Secondary connections:** [Where New Evidence Matters](/research/where-new-evidence-matters.html), [Modes of Climate Delivery](/research/modes-of-climate-delivery.html)

**Decision or problem:** How to distinguish sector changes from occupation transitions in place-based low-carbon workforce planning.

**Existing evidence:** Public occupational evidence used to examine relatedness and transition requirements.

**Consequential uncertainty:** Calibration choices affect which transition requirements and workforce burdens become visible.

**Delivery conditions:** Workforce institutions, skills systems and employers shape whether occupational transitions are feasible.

**Consequences examined:** Changes in occupations, skills requirements and access to low-carbon work.

**Evidence status:** Owner-approved programme description; the methodology is in development.

**Claim boundaries:** The work does not predict individual transitions or presume that all green employment is accessible or good work.

**Next learning question:** Which transition requirements are most consequential for workers and places?

## Research questions

- Which requirements distinguish sector changes from transitions between occupations?
- How can occupational relatedness and transition requirements be calibrated from public evidence?
